dct_description_sm: The main objective of this project was to collect information in order to enable the assessment and identification of the risks of sea level rise and coastal erosion in Nunavut.   This first part of the projects aimed to complete assessments in Hall Beach (the most vulnerable community in Nunavut to coastal erosion) and Clyde River. The project was intended to create capacity within the Ittaq Heritage and Research Centre in Clyde River to monitor local sea level rise and coastal erosion impacts (for future use in community action plans). The project was also designed to support the overall Nunavut Adaptation Plan using community case studies and to inform other coastal communities.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Adaptation
dct_title_s: Addressing Climate Change Adaptation: A Collaborative Approach in Support of the Nunavut Climate Change Adaptation Plan - Arctic Sea Level Rise and Coastal Impacts Assessment Project
